title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 52
paragraphs: Having so resolved, during that whole day they had unceasing trouble while the cavalry pressed them. But when the day drew to a close and the cavalry's attacks had ceased, then, as night was coming on and the hour arrived at which they had agreed to retire from their place, most of them set out and began to withdraw — but not keeping it in mind to go to the agreed place. On the contrary, once they had begun to move, they readily took the chance to flee from the cavalry toward the city of the Plataeans; and in their flight they came as far as the temple of Hera, which stands before the Plataean city, twenty furlongs from the spring Gargaphia. Having arrived there, they halted in front of the temple.
